text:
anya: quick brain dump — we need to design a tenant-aware hedging/fallback protocol. goals: per-tenant latency budgets, deterministic fallback stacks, minimal cross-tenant blast radius.
li: +1. do we want a centralized arbiter or local decisioning at the edge proxy?
sam: leaning local — faster, but harder to enforce global cost budgets.
jordan: local + central policy: local makes fast decisions using per-tenant SLO, central provides config and safety caps.
maria: what signals are we going to use? latency p50/p95, token-per-request, kv-cache-hit, GPU-queue-length, model-quality-regressions?
anya: yes. propose probe signals: last 30s p95, model-quality-regression hook (run evals on a small prompt set), backend queue depth, and CVE-like operator flags.
li: how do we avoid oscillation? need hysteresis + rate limit window. something like a token-leaky-bucket + cooldown per-tenant.
sam: also define a "fallback-stack": prioritized list of variants. e.g. same-model 8-bit -> quantized 6b -> smaller family -> cached_short -> synthetic degrade. fallback should be ordered and idempotent.
jordan: operator override + immutable audit trail required for enterprise customers. every auto-fallback event must log reason + pre/post routing state.
anya: API sketch for route-level config (very rough):
```json
{"route": "/v1/generate", "safepath": {"budget_ms": 200, "fallbacks": ["gptx-8q", "gptx-6b-quant", "cached_short"], "hysteresis_ms": 1000}}
```
li: runtime concerns: adding per-tenant state to the router increases memory. store only active-tenants in an LRU and persist policy in central config. cold-tenant requests fall back to central policy with default caps.
maria: cache priming order: when routing to a smaller model, spin up async prefix-KV warmup if warmup budget allows. avoid blocking the primary request unless budget is generous.
sam: session affinity question: some workflows need KV continuity. fallback should try to preserve affinity by preferring co-located smaller variants or falling back to cached responses that maintain session continuity when possible.
jordan: telemetry must include reason codes: "capacity", "latency", "quality_regression", "operator", "probe_failure". include model-version, route, tenant_id, and pre/post token-cost estimate.
anya: rollout plan: start with read-only canary (observability only) in a single region; then enable auto-fallback for a single high-traffic internal tenant for 48h; measure fallback triggers, cost delta, and customer-visible latency.
li: ops playbook: trigger page if fallback rate > 2% (or >500 events) for 10m OR cost delta > 15% sustained 30m. include automated rollback toggle.
maria: long-term refactor idea: split the router into a small, fast "decision plane" microservice (stateless cache + local signals) and a control-plane for policy distribution and simulation.
sam: the policy DSL should be deliberately small: conditions on signals (p95> X, queue>Y), actions (route/hedge/fallback), cooldowns and max-fallback-rate per minute. keep it evaluable in O(1) per request.
anya: tests: unit sim for non-oscillation, integration test for fallback-stack ordering, and chaos test where backend capacity drops 3x. small PRs: first add signal surface + logging, then local decision, then central caps.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: canary/tenant-hedge-v1 -> prod-canary scheduled 2026-04-01T16:00:00Z :rocket:
jordan: thanks all. I'll draft an RFC with the API, DSL sample, and a short sim harness.
anya: awesome — add a section on cost accounting per-fallback-event (token-level delta is important).
li: and include tests for hysteresis and eviction semantics in the RFC.
maria: +1
sam: lgtm
anya: closing this thread, will link the RFC when ready :thumbsup:
